predecessors.name: Sparta (Peloponnesian League)
predecessors.text: Messenia, the helot land of Sparta since the Messenian Wars

successors.name: Achaean League
successors.text: Messenia: 'Later Hypana in Elis, Corone, Messene, Sparta and Pagae ... were joined by conquest'

ledger.x: 369: Epaminondas founds Messene and Messenia is free of Sparta.
Nabis is driven out: 'the Spartans were forced to retreat when the Achaean League army under Philopoemen intervened'.

191: Messenia passes to the Achaean League and the independent Messene ends; Dinocrates' revolt of 183 ('encouraged Messene to revolt against the League') and the League's capture of the city are recorded in achaean-league (contest 183-182); the page's wording: 'the members of the Achaean League joined forces to…

wars.name: Nabis' capture of Messene
wars.outcome: Nabis captured Messene in 201 BC; the Spartans retreated when Philopoemen's Achaean army intervened.

certainty.note: No page dates a frontier of the Messenian polis; the line with Laconia, Arcadia and Elis is approximate throughout.
